Subject: Resale coverage for multiple ship-to entities

Hi Logan,

We're finalizing onboarding with Redwood and need to provide resale documentation so you can clear outstanding invoices for Q1. We have a couple of different 'ship-to' entities that move freight across states — some are subsidiaries and some are regional DBAs. Can you confirm what you need for each ship-to address so we can send the right certificates?

Short background: GreenVector operates as: 
- GreenVector Logistics, Inc. (parent EIN: 12-3456789)
- GV Freight Solutions (a wholly owned subsidiary; separate EIN)
- GreenVector Midwest (DBA used on POs)

We can provide PDF resale certificates and a signed attestation. Are you able to accept a single blanket certificate for the holding company, or do you need individual state forms per ship-to/EIN? Also flag if any states require notarization or additional signatory info.

Attaching the preliminary mapping we have (spreadsheet) for your reference.

Thanks,
Emily Turner
Senior Procurement Manager
GreenVector Logistics

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>

Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Feb 2027 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Resale coverage for multiple ship-to entities

Emily —

Thanks for the spreadsheet and the clear breakdown. Quick summary of what we need so our finance team can release invoices: 

- Per-entity EIN matching is preferred for invoice release. If you can provide state resale certificates that list the EIN used on the PO/Invoice (or a blanket certificate that explicitly names each DBA and EIN), that will speed validation.
- For Missouri (MO) and Texas (TX) we often need a signed state form rather than a generic blanket. MO sometimes expects a ship-to mapping (ship-to name + EIN).
- A signed attestation that the DBAs on the POs are covered by the parent entity's blanket is acceptable in many states; we will still request copies of the state's accepted form for MO/TX.

Mina (cc'd) is our tax evidence reviewer — she can confirm any state-specific requirements and whether notarization is necessary. I'll keep this thread in my inbox and forward to finance when we have the validated docs.

Next step: Emily, if you can upload the state PDFs and the signed attestation (or send back via DocuSign), Mina will review and I will coordinate with Sean in Finance to clear invoices.

Best,
Logan Wright
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.com
[Attachment: none]

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Emily Turner <emily.turner@gvlogistics.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 08:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Resale coverage for multiple ship-to entities

Emily / Logan —

I reviewed the mapping. To make our acceptance process deterministic, please provide the following for each ship-to: 

1) State-specific resale certificate PDF (signed) that either lists the ship-to name and EIN OR a blanket that explicitly enumerates DBAs and EINs.
2) A single-page attestation (signed) from an authorized signer confirming the relationship between parent and DBAs (if you provide a blanket for the parent).
3) A copy of one PO or invoice showing the ship-to name exactly as you want it mapped (helps avoid transcription mismatches).

If any of the ship-to entities operate in Missouri, please use the Missouri state form where possible — MO teams sometimes reject generic copies. If a state requires notarization I will call it out in my review, but that's uncommon for our typical SaaS resale acceptance.

Please send PDFs and include the EIN on the top-right of each form if possible. I will validate and reply with either "accepted" or the correction list per entity.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Tax Evidence Specialist, Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.com
